Expand your access with a residence permit

If your Chinese passport has limited reach, a residence permit can unlock many additional destinations. Pairing your passport with one of the permits below typically adds 5–15 new visa-free or visa-on-arrival countries:

  • UAE residence permit — strong for South Asian passport holders, unlocks Armenia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Serbia
  • US Green Card — unlocks Mexico, Canada (via eTA), several Caribbean and Central American countries
  • Schengen residence permit — unlocks Turkey, Balkans, several visa-free short stays across the EU

Frequently asked questions

How many countries can Chinese passport holders visit visa-free?
Chinese passport holders have visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to approximately 85 countries — 49 visa-free and 36 visa-on-arrival. Notable visa-free destinations include Albania, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Armenia, Azerbaijan.
Is the Chinese passport strong?
The Chinese passport is moderately powerful, covering 85 destinations for easy entry. Pairing it with a residence permit (UAE, Schengen, US Green Card) significantly expands access.
Do I need an ETA or e-visa for some countries?
Yes. 35 destinations require an e-visa (online application before arrival) for Chinese passport holders. These are typically quicker than embassy visas but still need to be arranged before travel.
Which countries require a full visa in advance?
78 countries require Chinese passport holders to obtain a visa from an embassy before travelling. Check the destination embassy's website for specific requirements and processing times.
Can a residence permit or second visa unlock extra countries?
Yes — several residence permits grant bonus visa-free access regardless of your Chinese passport. See our guides for UAE residence, US Green Card, and Schengen residence permit to learn which countries unlock for each.
How accurate is this list?
Entries marked with a ✓ badge have been re-verified against an official government source (embassy, ministry, or visa portal) and link to that source. Entries without the badge come from the community-maintained open-source Passport Index Dataset — a reasonable starting point but not individually verified. Rules change frequently. Always confirm with the destination embassy before booking travel.
